title: Risk sharing for background risk models with infinite mean
abstract: arXiv:2611.27485v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Risk sharing is usually viewed as beneficial for risk-averse agents facing independent risks with finite means, but this situation can be reversed for infinite-mean losses. In this paper, we explore the effects of risk sharing for positively dependent infinite-mean losses using background risk models. Under both linear and conditional mean risk sharing, we show that risk sharing of infinite-mean losses can increase the risk in the sense of usual stochastic order. Our results cover classical multivariate loss distributions, including the Pareto-Clayton and the Fr\'echet-Gumbel models. For linear risk sharing, we further derive stochastic dominance relations between diversified portfolios, including those with Pareto marginals coupled by convex mixtures of commonly used Archimedean copulas. tldr: 本文利用背景风险模型研究正相关的无限均值损失，证明在线性风险分担和条件均值风险分担下，风险分担可能在通常随机序的意义下反而增加风险，从而颠覆了风险分担总是有益的传统认知。
en_tdlr: Using background risk models for positively dependent infinite-mean losses, this paper shows that risk sharing under both linear and conditional mean schemes can increase risk in the sense of usual stochastic order, reversing the conventional belief that risk sharing is always beneficial.
